criteria: `render(template, values)` is implemented in `template.py`, takes a `dict` as `values`, and returns the template with each field replaced.

Rule 1: In `render`, a field is `{path}`, where a path is one or more names joined by dots (such as `user.name`) and a name is letters, digits and underscores; whitespace inside the braces around the path is ignored, so `{ user.name }` is the same field as `{user.name}`.

Rule 2: In `render`, the first name of a path is looked up in `values`, and each later name is looked up in the value found so far: as a key when that value is a `dict`, and as an index when it is a `list` or a `tuple` and the name is all digits (`items.0`); attribute lookup is never used.
Rule 3: In `render`, a found value is inserted as `str(value)`, except that `None` is inserted as the empty string, and `True` and `False` are inserted as `true` and `false`.

Rule 4: In `render`, `{path|text}` gives a default: when the lookup fails at any step, `text` is inserted exactly as written, spaces included, up to the closing brace; the default may be empty (`{name|}`); a value that is found and is `None` is not a failed lookup.
Rule 5: In `render`, a failed lookup with no default raises `KeyError` whose first argument is the full path as written in the field, trimmed, such as `"user.name"`.
Rule 6: In `render`, `{{` is a literal `{` and `}}` is a literal `}`; they are not fields.

Rule 7: `render` raises `ValueError` for: a `{` with no closing `}`, a `}` with no opening `{`, an empty field `{}`, a path that is not valid by rule 1 (such as `{a..b}` or `{a-b}`), and a `{` inside a field.
Rule 8: In `render`, text outside fields is copied unchanged, and inserted values are not scanned again for fields.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
